solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Drink factory one enters, begging (9)

indicatorNotes.enters: one goes into the factory, so I sits inside PLANT

annotation.surface: A thirsty worker at a drinks factory, pleading for a job.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Drink' reads as a noun heading a phrase about a drinks plant; it is the verb SUP, standing alone.
annotation.definitionFit: A suppliant person is one begging humbly, so the adjective matches 'begging'.

entries.clue: So much ice cream commonly sold in small supermarket (5)

annotation.definition: So much ice cream commonly sold in

blocks.note: S = small, as on clothing labels
the Co-op is a British supermarket chain

annotation.surface: Ice cream sold in a little corner shop.
annotation.walkthrough: The definition runs almost the whole clue: a scoop is the measure ice cream is usually sold in. The Co-op is a chain of British grocery shops.
annotation.definitionFit: A unit of measure, defined by use: the rounded ball a server lifts from the tub is how cones and cups are priced.

entries.clue: This jolting the Polo? (7)

indicatorNotes.jolting: jolting shakes the letters of THE POLO about

annotation.surface: A Volkswagen Polo bouncing along a ruined road.
annotation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both the wordplay and the definition: a pothole is what jolts a small car like the Polo, and THE POLO rearranged spells it. The Polo mint, famous for its hole, adds a second joke.
annotation.definitionFit: A pothole is a hole in the road that jolts any car passing over it.

entries.clue: WI group managed farm, charging tenants (6,8)

indicatorNotes.charging: to charge is to load or fill, so LESSEES are filled with RAN TILL

blocks.note: to till is to farm the soil

annotation.surface: A women's group running a farm and billing the people who rent from it.
annotation.walkthrough: WI looks like the Women's Institute, a British village club; here it is the West Indies. 'Charging' sounds like billing rent, and is the filling instruction.
annotation.definitionFit: The Lesser Antilles are a chain of islands in the West Indies.

entries.clue: Lake in spring rising where glaciers have melted (4)

indicatorNotes.in: the lake goes in the spring
indicatorNotes.rising: in a down clue, rising reads the letters upward

blocks.note: a spa is a mineral spring

annotation.surface: Meltwater from a glacier welling up in a lake.
annotation.walkthrough: SPA takes L inside to make SPLA, which reads upward as ALPS. The definition is loose on purpose: the Alps are a place whose glaciers have shrunk.
annotation.definitionFit: The Alps are a mountain range famous for glaciers that are now retreating.

entries.clue: Having three parties, suffering hosts delayed fourth for year (10)

indicatorNotes.hosts: TRIAL hosts, that is holds, the rest

blocks.note: a trial is an ordeal, a suffering

annotation.surface: A three-way arrangement held up by a long ordeal.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Fourth for year' asks for a single letter: count along the word 'year' to its fourth. 'Suffering' looks like an adjective in the surface, and is a noun here.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym built from Latin: three sides, used of treaties and talks with three participants.

entries.clue: Lighter selection from Tesco welcomed (4)

indicatorNotes.selection from: a selection is a run of letters picked from the words that follow

annotation.surface: A lighter being picked off the shelf at Tesco, the supermarket.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Lighter' suggests a cigarette lighter for sale at the supermarket; it is a flat barge. Tesco is a British supermarket chain.
annotation.definitionFit: A lighter is a flat-bottomed barge for unloading ships, and a scow is one.

entries.clue: Examiner questioning how someone passed? (7)

blocks.note: reads as someone who sets or marks exams; it is an official who examines deaths
reads as quizzing a candidate on their success; 'passed' means passed away, and the questioning is an inquest

annotation.surface: A marker quizzing a student on how they got through a test.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Passed' suggests an exam, which 'Examiner' reinforces; it means died, and the examiner holds inquests.
annotation.definitionFit: A coroner is the official who investigates the cause of a sudden or unexplained death.

entries.clue: Still second behind cycling cheat (8)

indicatorNotes.cycling: cycling moves the first letter of SWINDLE round to the back
indicatorNotes.behind: the S for second goes after

annotation.surface: A cyclist who still cheats, finishing second.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Still' at the front reads as an adverb meaning 'even now'; it is the adjective for calm weather.
annotation.definitionFit: A weather sense: a still day is one with no breeze at all.

entries.clue: Pull and haul up ropes aboard ship, being very slack? (14)

indicatorNotes.up: in a down clue, up reads the letters from the bottom
indicatorNotes.aboard: the pieces go on board SS, the steamship

blocks.note: lines are ropes on a ship

annotation.surface: Sailors heaving ropes on deck, accused of idling.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is all hard effort on deck, while the answer is its opposite: laziness. 'Ship' as SS, for steamship, is a crossword staple.
annotation.definitionFit: Sluggardliness is the state of being a sluggard, lazy and very slack.

entries.clue: Anything you hear in Yorkshire’s inaccurate (3)

indicatorNotes.you hear: the sound of the word is wanted

blocks.note: owt is northern English dialect for anything

annotation.walkthrough: In Yorkshire speech, owt means anything and nowt means nothing. Said aloud, owt matches OUT.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: an estimate that is off by some margin is said to be out by that much.

entries.clue: Italian player substituted sooner given bottle to carry (6,5)

indicatorNotes.substituted: the letters of SOONER swap places
indicatorNotes.to carry: the rearranged letters carry PHIAL inside them

blocks.note: a phial is a small bottle

annotation.surface: A footballer from Italy coming off the bench early and given a drink.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Player' and 'substituted' make a football scene, but the player is an actor, and 'substituted' only shuffles letters.
annotation.definitionFit: Sophia Loren is an Italian film actress, and an actor is a player.

entries.clue: Humbug, penny sweet (6)

blocks.note: honey is sweet, and a term of endearment

annotation.surface: A list of cheap sweets: a humbug, a penny chew.
annotation.walkthrough: A humbug is a British boiled mint sweet, which fits the sweet-shop picture; here it is a fraud.
annotation.definitionFit: A dated sense of humbug: a fraud or impostor, as in Scrooge's 'Bah, humbug!' for Christmas cheer he thinks fake.

entries.clue: Migrant alarming at the border (8)

indicatorNotes.Migrant: a migrant moves, so the letters of ALARMING move too

annotation.surface: A news line about a frightening scene at a frontier.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Migrant' looks like the subject of a news story, and it is only the instruction to move the letters of the next word.
annotation.definitionFit: Marginal means lying at the edge or border.

entries.clue: Proper wish maybe taking form of prayer? (10)

annotation.definition: Proper wish maybe taking form of prayer?

indicatorNotes.taking form: the letters of PROPER WISH take a new form

annotation.surface: A well-meant wish that turns into a prayer.
annotation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines too: someone whose proper wish becomes a prayer is a worshipper.
annotation.definitionFit: A worshipper is one who prays, turning wishes into prayer.

entries.clue: Deadly unit evacuated by hospital — never mind (3,5)

indicatorNotes.evacuated by: the hospital leaves LETHAL, taking its H with it

blocks.note: H = hospital, as on road signs

annotation.surface: A dangerous ward cleared of patients, then shrugged off.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Evacuated by' means the hospital leaves the word, taking its letter with it. The definition is the phrase used to rule something out: 'I can't boil an egg, never mind cook dinner'.
annotation.definitionFit: Let alone and never mind are interchangeable in 'not a penny, let alone a pound'.

entries.clue: Large amount in account, others short (5)

indicatorNotes.short: REST falls short by its last letter

blocks.note: REST (the others) without its last letter

annotation.surface: A big sum in a bank account, while others go short.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Acres of' means lots of, as in acres of space.
annotation.definitionFit: An informal idiom: 'acres of space' or 'acres of print' means a great deal, borrowing the land measure.

entries.clue: Republican party ties do very well (2,6)

blocks.note: the GOP, Grand Old Party, is the US Republican Party

annotation.surface: Politicians in party ties thriving.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Ties' could be neckwear or links; it is the verb, to lace.
annotation.definitionFit: Someone who will go places is set to succeed, to do very well.

entries.clue: Did champ taking gold first complete circuits? (5)

indicatorNotes.first: the gold goes in front of the rest

blocks.note: to champ is to bite, so 'did champ' is BIT

annotation.surface: A champion winning gold after running laps.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Champ' is the verb to bite, not a champion; 'did' puts it in the past tense.
annotation.definitionFit: To orbit is to go round and round, completing circuits.

entries.clue: History smashed Boney’s grand forces apart (7)

annotation.definitionNote: BYGONES is plural; 'history' is a singular noun for the same past things

indicatorNotes.smashed: something smashed is broken into pieces, so the letters of BONEYS are broken and reassembled
indicatorNotes.forces apart: G pushes in and splits the rearranged letters

annotation.surface: Napoleon's great army broken up and consigned to history.
annotation.walkthrough: Boney was the British nickname for Napoleon, which makes this read as a battle report; 'forces' looks like his army, and is a verb.
annotation.definitionFit: Bygones are things past, which is what history is.

entries.clue: Basket lost below clothes son put outside room, finally (4,4)

indicatorNotes.clothes: SUNK wraps round the rest like clothing
indicatorNotes.put outside: whatever is put outside something ends up surrounding it, so the son wraps round the room's last letter

blocks.note: a ship that is sunk is lost below the waves
a lad is a boy, a son

annotation.surface: A laundry basket lost under a son's clothes, dumped outside his room.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Clothes' looks like laundry in a basket and is a verb, to dress or wrap. The basket is a score in basketball, not a laundry basket.
annotation.definitionFit: A slam dunk is a basket scored by jamming the ball down through the hoop.

entries.clue: Close relationship warmer in bed? (7)

annotation.surface: A close couple keeping each other warm in bed.
annotation.walkthrough: The definition is playful: a nightie is a garment that keeps you warm in bed.
annotation.definitionFit: A nightie is a nightdress, worn to keep warm in bed.

entries.clue: Money provided in case member bet on ace (5,3)

indicatorNotes.on: in an across clue, LAID comes on after the A

blocks.note: a leg is a limb, a member
A = ace, as on playing cards
to lay a bet: laid = bet

annotation.surface: Cash put by just in case, then gambled on an ace.
annotation.walkthrough: 'In case' sounds like 'as a precaution'; the case is a legal one.
annotation.definitionFit: Legal aid is public money that pays for a lawyer in a court case.

entries.clue: Evil German hit interpreter, perhaps (6)

annotation.surface: A wicked German striking a translator.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Hit' looks like a blow and 'interpreter' a translator; a singer interprets hit songs.
annotation.definitionFit: A singer performs, or interprets, songs such as hits.

entries.clue: Due and true correspond in sound (5)

indicatorNotes.in sound: the answer matches 'correspond' only when spoken

blocks.note: a noun here: what you are owed or entitled to
true in the sense of correct
to correspond is to write letters

annotation.surface: Two rhyming words said to match in sound.
annotation.walkthrough: Three routes to one word: two meanings and one sound. 'Correspond in sound' looks like a comment on due and true rhyming.
annotation.definitionFit: What you are due is your right, and what is true is right.

entries.clue: A little Jacob male that needs raising? (4)

annotation.definition: A little Jacob male that needs raising?

indicatorNotes.A little: just a small part of the words is used
indicatorNotes.needs raising: in a down clue, raising reads the letters upward

annotation.surface: A young ram of the Jacob breed that has to be reared.
annotation.walkthrough: Jacob is a British breed of spotted sheep, so a little Jacob male needing to be raised is a lamb; the hidden letters read upward spell it.
annotation.definitionFit: A lamb is a young sheep, such as a Jacob, that must be reared.

entries.clue: Study chapter that discusses basis for subsequent work (11)

blocks.note: a book on a subject discusses it
a template is a pattern for later work

annotation.surface: A textbook chapter laying the groundwork for what follows.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Study' reads as a noun heading an academic phrase; it is the verb.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym for the verb: to look at or think about something long and carefully.

entries.clue: Yank instinctively felt repelled (3)

indicatorNotes.repelled: driven back, so the letters run backwards

blocks.note: a gut feeling is felt instinctively

annotation.surface: An American who sensed he was being pushed away.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Yank' looks like an American; it is the verb, to pull sharply.
annotation.definitionFit: A tug is a sudden hard pull, a yank.

entries.clue: Discover son with decapitated cat (4)

indicatorNotes.decapitated: the head, first letter, comes off PUSS

annotation.surface: A grisly find: a boy with a headless cat.
annotation.walkthrough: To suss, or suss out, is British slang for working something out.
annotation.definitionFit: British slang, short for suspect: to suss out a plan is to find out what is going on.

entries.clue: Smear cologne on mate’s back, blushing (9)

indicatorNotes.on: the cologne goes on after the E
indicatorNotes.back: the back of MATE is its last letter

blocks.note: to rub on is to smear

annotation.surface: Someone going red while rubbing cologne onto a partner's back.
annotation.walkthrough: The rare word is Latin-based: rubescent means turning red.
annotation.definitionFit: Rubescent means reddening, as a face does when blushing.
